summary: Built the hand-off for the person's whole-C:\ W-001 run, and nothing else in product or case code. It is a new page, docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md, with two sentences added to SL-089-seams.md. The counts-only rule is widened from the first draft to a closed grammar, with a 44-row corpus and a runner. A tests/bugs/SL-107-HandOffCases.ps1 script covers C-001 to C-006, and C-007 and C-008 are corpus rows F12 and F02 of the existing W001OracleTests. One unplanned fix was needed: the engine-appended rule matches no file until the record exists, which made the rules harness's clean baseline exit 2. The harness now allows a rule listed under awaiting_file to match nothing while its file is absent, and plants.json carries real-engine rows for the rule. The whole-C:\ run itself was not made: it is the person's, and no engine stage may make it.

files.why: The person's page: reasons the run is theirs (the 0.5 GB and 3 GB figures disagree, under both), pre-flight, the teed command with the artifacts folder made first, a table of endings, the record fields for criteria 1-4, the Q-261 reconciliation with the same-session floor, what to commit, and a result table (M1, M2).
Two sentences beside the command: use pwsh with -Root C:\ because the cmd.exe form arrives as C:" and stops with nothing written, and a pointer to the SL-107 page.

The engine-appended settled rule over the committed record: first pattern replaced by a closed grammar (any slash, any backslash that is not a JSON quote or code-unit escape, the u005c and u002f spellings), the path key pattern kept, because-text updated (m1).
Corpus closing the class of path spellings without a drive letter: 44 rows, each with the first draft's hit count, plus the residual false negatives named.

Reads the patterns from fitness.yaml and applies them to every corpus row. Checks the writer and the rule agree by loading Write-W001Record from WindowCases.ps1, and applies the rule to any record on this machine.
Cases C-001 to C-006 as runnable checks: the cmd.exe form, the seams doc, the SL-107 doc, W-001 over D:\, over the tree holding the layer store, and over the fsa-guard-tests fixtures.

load_awaiting plus check_clean/describe_unmatched: a rule listed under awaiting_file may match no file in the clean baseline only while its file is absent from the scratch copy. Without it the baseline exits 2.
awaiting_file entry for the rule; rows S83-S86 (must fire) and P36 (a whole real record, must stay quiet) so the engine's own Fitness is run on the rule (m2); the note's counts and history updated.
Design record kept in step: the rule's patterns and because-text, and would_force_resynthesis false with the 0.5 GB / 3 GB disagreement kept as a recorded fact (m3, O-015).

obligations.how: Case C-001 is built and passes: tests/bugs/SL-107-HandOffCases.ps1 -Case C-001. It first proves through an echo script that the cmd.exe line delivers C:" (otherwise nothing runs, so it can never start a whole-drive scan). Then it runs the real cmd.exe line and checks exit 1, 'C:" is not a folder', 'FAILED: W-001', no 'PASSED', and the C record unchanged (absent).

Case C-002 passes: it extracts the section 'Criterion 3 on C:\ is a person's run' of SL-089-seams.md and checks it names cmd.exe, what arrives, the pointer to SL-107-c-drive-run.md and the unchanged command.

Case C-003 passes: the SL-107 doc holds every required string (command, Tee-Object, the capture file, the three endings, TIMEOUT, LEAK:, openRefusedButOpenable, notScanned, leftoverRows) plus the M1 and M2 contents and the guard-disagreement section.

Case C-004 passes: W-001 -Root D:\ ends PASSED, exit 0, record names artifacts/w001-run.json, scope whole-drive, verdict held, rows 2 = header 2 = coreUnreadable 2, and the C record is unchanged (absent).

Case C-005 passes: W-001 over C:/ProgramData/Microsoft/Windows ends PASSED with notScanned 1, 449 rows = header = coreUnreadable, openRefusedButOpenable 0, verdict held (the header's 'not scanned (1)' suffix parsed).
Case C-006 passes: W-001 over the fsa-guard-tests fixtures gives 27 rows, all code-363 leftovers, reparse 0, notARefusedKeepShape empty, openedNothingListed 0, oracle.opened 0.

Existing test, row F12 (code 1920, NothingListed, expected other-code) of W001OracleCorpus.json in FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.W001OracleTests.TheOracleGivesEveryRowOfTheCorpusItsClass, passes (1/1). No new test was needed; the doc states the 1920 row lands only under notARefusedKeepShape.

Existing test, row F02 (code 5, listable folder, expected leak) of the same corpus Fact, passes in the same run (1/1). The doc's endings table describes the LEAK: line and the corpus-first fix (lesson 361).

M1 built in docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md: the place is 'a checkout of the branch that carries SL-107's merge' (main on uat once merged), the record is committed on that branch, and New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force artifacts | Out-Null comes before the Tee-Object line. Measured that Tee-Object does not create a missing parent folder ('Could not find a part of the path'). The teed command shape ran on C:/Windows/Logs: PASSED, $LASTEXITCODE 0, capture of 85 lines with the record: and PASSED lines.

M2 built: section 5 of the doc replaces 'no hard floor' with a floor measured in the same session. After the C:\ run the person runs W-001 over C:/Windows, C:/ProgramData and the user's Temp, copying each record to anchor-windows.json, anchor-programdata.json and anchor-temp.json. The C: rows must be at least their sum (each of the Temp anchor and the C: run carries its own control-denied row, so the +1 cancels). Code 363 is compared with the Temp anchor's day count, the remainder is named, and the old Layers share is stated as unmeasurable because the path lists are gone. A result table is in the doc.

m1 fixed beyond its literal fix, as a closed grammar: '/' ; any backslash not followed by a quote or u, plus u005c and u002f escapes; the path key kept. The extra backslash alternative is needed because a single-backslash path typed by hand (C:\temp\new) is valid JSON and the pair-of-backslashes pattern misses it. Corpus tests/bugs/SL-107-RecordPathRuleCorpus.json: 44 rows over drive-letter, row-key, UNC, relative, variable-rooted, hand-typed, escaped-separator, residual and record families. The first draft's patterns fail 21 rows (shown in a scratch copy; each row's recorded first-draft count is verified live), and the corpus agrees under Python re with the patterns the engine loads. The writer and the rule agree on every writer row.

m2 built through the repo's harness so the engine's own Fitness runs: plants.json rows S83 (UNC), S84 (single-backslash typed path), S85 (relative, forward slashes), S86 (dumped row with a path key) fire and P36 (a whole real record) stays quiet, all AS-RECORDED, 0 strays. The clean baseline needed the awaiting_file allowance (harness.py) to be clean at all. With the slash pattern removed the harness exits 1 (S85 MISSED-BY-FITNESS; with the other pattern also reverted S83 and S84 miss too). RuleCases -Case All passed (407 s).

The design record now has would_force_resynthesis false for the pool-guard disagreement, with the sentence kept as a recorded fact (older docs say 0.5 GB per run, the engine's watch stops at 3 GB, this slice depends on neither). The SL-107 doc's reason section does not rest on 0.5 GB: it gives the brief naming the run the owner's, the need for the person's allowance, the 537 MB measurement against the 3-4.4 GiB prediction, and pool kept until a restart. It adds that the two figures disagree and the run is the person's under both. WindowCases.ps1 is untouched; SL-089-seams.md has only the two planned sentences.
obligations.not_mutable: A flag in the engine's exported design record (overwritten from the engine store on refresh, Q-106) and a paragraph of the doc; no test observes the flag. The doc's reason section is checked by case C-003 (the 0.5 GB / 3 GB / 537 MB / 3-4.4 GiB / restart strings).

mandatory.where: docs/design/SL-107-c-drive-run.md section 5 builds Q-261's decision: criterion 5 is met by reconciliation with notScanned exactly 1, code 363 27-28, code 1920 0-2, rows at most 682 (about 660), and every difference from 682 named by path group (a to f). A same-session floor (three bounded anchor runs) was added so a shortfall cannot be hidden under 'Layers'. A count outside the ranges, or an unnamed gap, is stated to be a scanner finding. The record itself is the person's run.

deviations: The design said change no code. The engine-appended counts-only rule matches no file until the person commits the record, and the repo's harness (eng/rules-harness/harness.py) refuses a clean baseline with an unmatched rule: it exited 2 on this tree, and RuleCases C-007 and Q-027's validate run would fail with it. I added a small allowance, awaiting_file in plants.json, read by load_awaiting and check_clean. A listed rule may match nothing only while its file is absent from the scratch copy. Both ends were checked: present-but-unmatched still blocks (exit 2), and unlisted-unmatched still blocks. RuleCases -Case All passed.

m1's literal fix ('\\\\|/') was widened to a closed grammar (any slash, any backslash that is not a JSON quote or code-unit escape, the u005c/u002f spellings). Reason: a path typed with single backslashes (C:\temp\new) is valid JSON and the pair pattern misses it; the corpus shows it. This is what the CLOSE THE CLASS obligation asks for.

The rule's engine check (m2) was built as harness plant rows (S83-S86, P36) rather than as a validate-time scratch step, and the design's 'add no code/tests' became two runnable scripts in tests/bugs. The owed cases C-001 to C-006 need commands the engine can run; a doc check alone feeds no shape.

The design record .taad/slices/SL-107/design-slice-1.json was edited as the builder instruction required (patterns, would_force_resynthesis). It is an engine export and may be overwritten on refresh (Q-106).

No workaround, setting or notice was added: the run depends on the existing wcifs-layer-store entry (outside defect in wcifs.sys). Both positions of its switch and the on-screen notice are covered by the existing cases, which I ran: X-004 (store left out, 'not scanned', the notice beside the totals) and X-005 (off through the confirmation, on again next launch).
not_built: The whole-C:\ W-001 run and the record .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json: the person's run (SC-136, SC-138). Nothing was run on whole C:\, and no engine stage may.

Cases C-009 to C-013 (timeout, elevated shell, precaution off, app stopped mid-scan, -Root C: without backslash, committed file holding a path): marked not material in the design and needing a click, an elevated session, a 20-minute run or a code change. Their code paths are read in the doc; the committed-path case is covered by the rule and its corpus.
Exposing the refused-then-listed count in the schema-1 report (Core and report change, scanner tier): filed for later in the design.

Raising the 1,200 s wait in Test-W001 or editing the guard comment at WindowCases.ps1 lines 6199-6200: not needed, and any edit to that file makes WindowMutants -Mutant All a required validate check (Q-114).
Any edit to .taad/slices/SL-089/index.json: an export of the engine store (Q-106).
An architecture-record edit: no block's sentence became untrue.
follow_ups: Once the person's record is committed, the awaiting_file entry in plants.json can be dropped (the rule then matches a real file); keeping it is harmless.
The harness's awaiting_file allowance has no RuleCases case of its own: it is covered by C-007 and by a manual negative run (listed file present but unmatched exits 2). A RuleCases case would pin it.
If the person's run ends TIMEOUT, raise the 1,200 literal in Invoke-HookedRun 'rows' inside Test-W001 (then run WindowMutants -Mutant All per Q-114).
Expose the refused-then-listed count (LastAccessAsked minus Kept minus Unreadable.Count, per U-102) in the report so a W-001 record can show the roughly 306,000 context figure.
Reconcile the per-run pool guard figure (0.5 GB in older docs, 3 GB in the engine's watch) in lesson #357 and SL-089-seams.md when convenient; this slice depends on neither.
